disease_label_per_paper: Cranial giant cell arteritis uncovered by PET/CT during fever of unknown origin evaluation
presentation_summary: 82-year-old man with dyslipidemia, hypertension, and glaucoma presented with a 3-week history of fever of unknown origin and rash.
Physical exam showed erythematous papular rash over the trunk; fatigue and weight loss were recorded.
Labs showed hemoglobin 7.6 g/dL, thrombocytosis 600 x10^3/uL, ferritin 1300 ng/mL, and ESR 120 mm/h.
Serologic tests for infectious agents and rheumatoid panels were non-diagnostic.

PET/CT showed FDG uptake in cranial and extracranial vessels including superficial temporal, maxillary, vertebral, occipital, subclavian, brachial, femoral, popliteal, and tibial arteries; glucocorticoid treatment led to rapid improvement.

confirmatory_findings.finding: PET/CT pattern of cranial and extracranial vessel involvement compatible with GCA
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: PET/CT showed involvement of cranial and extra-cranial vessels including superficial temporal, maxillary, vertebral and occipital arteries, as well as medium size vessels such as subclavian, brachial, femoral, and tibial arteries

confirmatory_findings.finding: Temporal artery ultrasound not diagnostic despite PET/CT pattern
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: ultrasound ... and cytological findings of the temporal arteries were non-remarkable ... Based on the widespread distribution and typical pattern on PET/CT, a diagnosis of giant cell arteritis was made
Glucocorticoid treatment was started, followed by a rapid and marked improvement of symptoms and inflammatory markers

quality_warnings: PET/CT vascular uptake is stored in confirmatory_findings, not ordinary observations, per D-GCA case-evidence rule.
The ordinary presentation evidence is a nonspecific fever-of-unknown-origin syndrome; current presentation-only smoke tests should not require D-GCA without consuming confirmatory PET/CT evidence.
Rash is structured because it was a presenting physical finding, but it is not treated as a core GCA-specific axis.
